book_product_page.seo_title: Read the Dollar First | USD Impact Book
book_product_page.meta_description: A compliance-safe macro-finance book explaining how the dollar regime transmits into oil, gold, Bitcoin, gas, FX, equities and market regimes.
book_product_page.hero: Most investors watch markets asset by asset. This book teaches a different starting point: read the dollar regime first.
book_product_page.subhero: Learn how dollar direction, real rates, liquidity stress and funding conditions transmit into oil, gold, Bitcoin, gas, FX, equities and broader market regimes.
sections: Markets rarely move in isolation. A stronger dollar can pressure commodities, a funding shock can lift the dollar and gold together, and falling DXY can mean very different things depending on whether real rates, liquidity or growth are leading the move. The book gives readers a clean framework for separating those regimes.

The reader learns why USD is not the same as DXY, why FX weakness is not the same as loss of purchasing power, how to read dollar regimes with three macro dials, and how those regimes affect oil, gas, gold, Bitcoin, equities and FX.
New and intermediate investors, market observers, client-facing market educators and sales teams that need a clear macro framework without turning the material into trading advice.
This is not a signal service, portfolio recommendation, forecast product or trading course. It is an educational framework for reading cross-asset conditions more clearly.

start_here.seo_title: Start Here | Learn How the Dollar Moves Markets
start_here.meta_description: The beginner route through USD Impact: learn what the dollar is, why DXY is limited, how to separate FX from inflation, and how to read dollar regimes.
start_here.h1: Start Here: Read the Dollar Before You Read the Asset
start_here.hero: USD Impact starts with one rule: define the dollar before interpreting the market move.
steps: Step 1 - Separate the meanings of USD
The dollar can mean a national currency, an exchange-rate instrument, a reserve asset, a funding currency and a liquidity refuge. Do not compress all of those meanings into one chart.
Step 2 - Do not confuse USD with DXY
DXY is useful, but it is a narrow index built around six developed-market currencies. It is not the entire dollar system.
Step 3 - Separate FX weakness from purchasing-power loss
A weaker dollar against other currencies and inflation inside the United States are different phenomena. They can overlap, but they should not be treated as synonyms.
Dollar moves can be led by rates, real yields, liquidity stress, relative growth, positioning or basket composition. The asset reaction depends on the driver.
Step 5 - Apply the framework to assets
Once the driver is clear, interpret oil, gas, gold, Bitcoin, equities and FX through the relevant transmission channel.

three_dial_dashboard.meta_description: A weekly dashboard for reading USD direction, real rates and liquidity stress before interpreting asset moves.
three_dial_dashboard.hero: A weekly operating framework for reading the dollar regime before interpreting cross-asset price action.
dials: Check DXY, broad USD, EURUSD and USDJPY. Confirm whether the move is broad or mostly a basket/composition move.
Check real yields and the curve. A dollar move driven by real rates can affect growth assets differently than a dollar move driven by liquidity stress.
Check volatility, credit spreads and funding indicators. Stress can lift the dollar even when the macro story looks negative.
